learning_objective: 🎯 Become a meteorologist! Learn why the wind blows, how global pressure belts control the weather, and what causes massive cyclones and storms.

main_concepts.simple_explanation: Air has weight! It pushes down on us. Hot air expands and rises, creating Low Pressure. Cold air condenses and sinks, creating High Pressure. Wind is simply air moving from High Pressure areas to Low Pressure areas.

Because the Earth is spinning, winds don't travel in a straight line. They are deflected (pushed off course) to the right in the Northern Hemisphere and to the left in the Southern Hemisphere. This invisible push is the Coriolis Force.

The Earth has distinct bands of high and low pressure. The equator is a low-pressure belt (warm). The poles are high-pressure belts (cold). This setup drives the permanent planetary winds like Trade Winds and Westerlies.

An Air Mass is a huge body of air with a uniform temperature. When a cold air mass crashes into a warm air mass, they don't mix easily. The boundary is called a 'Front', which often creates storms and Extra-Tropical Cyclones.

fun_activity.title: 🌀 The Spinning Coin
fun_activity.instructions: Place a coin flat on a table. Try to draw a straight line away from the center using a marker, but while drawing, slowly spin the coin with your other hand. Your 'straight' line will look curved on the coin! That is the Coriolis Effect in action.

exam_tips: 📌 Wind always flows from High Pressure to Low Pressure. The speed of the wind depends on the 'Pressure Gradient' (the steepness of the pressure difference).
📌 The ITCZ (Inter Tropical Convergence Zone) is a low-pressure zone near the equator where the northeast and southeast trade winds meet.
📌 Tropical cyclones require a warm ocean surface (above 27°C) and the presence of the Coriolis force to start spinning (which is why they don't form exactly at the equator).
quick_recap: ⭐ Wind direction is controlled by the Pressure Gradient Force, Coriolis Force, and Friction.
⭐ The Coriolis force deflects winds to the right in the North and left in the South.
⭐ A Front is the battleground between a warm air mass and a cold air mass.
